articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed; avg 12 published per cycle; 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active and the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05, for the stage-runner refactor) bars a new one, even though multi-source missed its target; nothing was evaluated or changed.
weakestArea: Multi-source fell to 26% (16 of 61) from 38% yesterday, 4 points under the 30% target. Today's mix leaned toward single-outlet stories that no wire picks up: Chinese tech press (Zhidx, TMTPost, TechNode), niche investigations (404 Media, Candiru, Telegram court records) and regional outlets (Kloop, Mada Masr, Premium Times). That is one day after a 38% day, so it reads as noise, not drift. If it stays under 30% across the pause, the 2026-05-09 floor raise was already tried and reverted, so the next lever would be on the feed side (event enrichment), not the selector floors.
watching: Gulf war: two ships sank near Hormuz, drones and missiles hit Yanbu and Riyadh, Trump threatened a MOAB strike on buried Iranian nuclear sites and Iran says Hormuz stays closed.
Russia sanctions: the US weighs easing shadow-fleet tanker sanctions while Ukraine says it has run out of Patriot interceptors.
Brazil runoff: prosecutors probe Meta and X over blocked Lula posts, a Lula hoax spread on X, and Maré polling stations were moved.
Gaza and the West Bank: Israel halted commercial goods into Gaza, and settlers beat olive pickers and a Washington Post photographer.
Markets: MSCI's rules eject bitcoin-treasury firms, Indonesia faces an emerging-market downgrade, and China's central bank keeps buying gold.
Mauritius extended its curfew after the worst unrest since 1999.
Alberta's independence referendum campaign is under way, with Carney leading the remain side.
coverageGaps: Oceania had no datelines for a third day running.
Africa fell to 3 datelines from 5 (Nigeria and Sudan); the Zambian copper settlement was datelined Abu Dhabi.
Science held at 6, just over the 5 floor; the sources were Phys.org, New Scientist, Carbon Brief and MIT Technology Review, with no Nature, Science or STAT findings.
Eight stories carry a country, not a city, as their location (six 'United States', plus 'China', 'Israel', 'United Kingdom'); the dateline rule wants the city.
context: All five cycles completed in 985s on average (selector 158s, writer 153s, editor 68s). Two stories rest only on state or advocacy sources (the EU anti-coercion tool against China and the Baniyas massacre arrests); both are allowed and labelled. Image URLs dropped to 97% from 100%, which is within noise.
